1.why: UI uses a clean sans-serif typeface with comfortable letter and line spacing across all screens.

2.why: Instructions use sentence case, no italics or all-caps, and appear as short single lines rather than dense blocks.

3.why: Layout is a single narrow card column with large controls that fits and remains readable at mobile width.

4.why: Copy such as “Sign in to begin. Take your time.” and “Enter the same contact details again.” is short and plain.

5.why: Step 1 shows explicit demo examples under each field (e.g. marcus@example.com, 07123 456789, MarcusDemo!54).

6.why: No screen requires reading a long paragraph; only brief labels and one-line hints are shown.

7.why: No long codes or secrets are ever presented, so no copy-to-clipboard control for them appears.

8.why: No QR code or equivalent alternative to manual entry is offered on any screen.

9.why: Standard labeled email/password inputs are used, which browsers and password managers can autofill, though no explicit autocomplete attributes are visible.

10.why: Header shows “Step X of 6” plus a prominent blue primary button that clearly marks the main action.

11.why: Each screen has exactly one solid primary button (Sign in and continue / Confirm my identity).

12.why: After login a green banner states “You are signed in. Next, confirm your identity,” but the later error state gives no plain next-step guidance.

13.why: Hints say “You can retry any step” and “You can correct and retry these details,” though reveal/hide/re-request of codes is never shown.

14.why: The only error shown is the technical message “Invalid array length,” which neither explains the problem in user terms nor how to fix it.

15.why: UI explicitly states “No reading timer. You can retry any step” and “Take your time,” with no countdown visible.
